run.question: We noticed our metrics dashboard shows missing data. Can you analyze the app-189-metrics-timeseries index to find any gaps in the data collection? When did data stop being collected and when did it resume? Also, what was the last request ID before the gap started?

report.summary: The app-189-metrics-timeseries index shows one clear collection gap inside the authorized window (2026-11-21T10:24:58Z to 2026-11-22T10:24:58Z). The index holds 18 documents in that window, all metric_name=cpu_usage, written once per hour at :23:00. The last document before the gap is at 2026-11-22T00:23:00Z with request_id REQ-37-8A4F2 (host server-3, value 41.0). The subsequent hourly buckets 01:00, 02:00, 03:00, 04:00, 05:00 and 06:00 on 2026-11-22 each contain zero documents, so six expected hourly samples are missing and no backfill exists; collection resumed with the sample at 2026-11-22T07:23:00Z with request_id REQ-2052-9284 (host server-5, value 20.0). Data therefore stopped being written after 2026-11-22T00:23:00Z (first missed slot 01:23:00Z) and resumed at 2026-11-22T07:23:00Z, a roughly seven-hour interruption. The cause of the interruption is not established by the available evidence: Prometheus was unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on both a range and an instant query), the otel-collector logs could not be read back to the gap interval because of the 4 MiB read limit, Kubernetes events exist only for 09:32-10:07Z, and no ConfigMap or Deployment matching app-189 or an Elasticsearch/indexer/exporter configuration was found. The only side observation is that the last pre-gap document's request_id (REQ-37-8A4F2) does not follow the REQ-NNNN-NNNN pattern used by every preceding sample in the window (for example REQ-1244-9615).

claims.text: The index app-189-metrics-timeseries exists, is green and open, and has a mapping of @timestamp (date), host (keyword), metric_name (keyword), request_id (keyword) and value (float).

Inside the authorized window (2026-11-21T10:24:58Z to 2026-11-22T10:24:58Z) the index returned 18 documents, all with metric_name=cpu_usage, min @timestamp 2026-11-21T11:23:00Z and max @timestamp 2026-11-22T10:23:00Z, written on an hourly cadence at :23:00.

The hourly date_histogram over @timestamp with min_doc_count=0 shows doc_count 1 for 2026-11-22T00:00Z, doc_count 0 for each of the 2026-11-22T01:00Z, 02:00Z, 03:00Z, 04:00Z, 05:00Z and 06:00Z buckets, and doc_count 1 again for 2026-11-22T07:00Z; no document exists with a timestamp inside the gap interval.
The last metric sample before the gap is the document at 2026-11-22T00:23:00Z with request_id REQ-37-8A4F2, host server-3 and value 41.0.

Collection resumed with the document at 2026-11-22T07:23:00Z with request_id REQ-2052-9284, host server-5 and value 20.0; the samples that follow it are 08:23:00Z (REQ-2149-7956), 09:23:00Z (REQ-2219-1109) and 10:23:00Z (REQ-2327-0978).

The request_id of the last pre-gap document, REQ-37-8A4F2, has a different format from every earlier sample in the window, which use the pattern REQ-NNNN-NNNN (e.g. REQ-1244-9615, REQ-0034-9386); the samples after the gap return to that pattern (REQ-2052-9284).

Each hourly document carries exactly one host and the host rotates: over the 18 in-window documents the counts are server-1 4, server-2 4, server-3 4, server-5 4 and server-4 2, so per-host continuity cannot be assessed from this index beyond the single rotating writer.

The otel-collector pod otel-collector-789c64b9bf-tl55c in namespace otel-demo is currently Running with restartCount 2 and lastState terminated reason Unknown; this is current pod state and the restart timestamps are not exposed, so it cannot be dated to the gap.

No Kubernetes event was returned in the gap interval: the only events inside the authorized window are 2 events grouped as involvedObject.kind=Endpoints, namespace null, reason=FailedToCreateEndpoint, and the event source range returned is 2026-11-22T09:32:52Z to 2026-11-22T10:07:47Z, which neither documents nor contradicts any change at 2026-11-22T00:23Z-07:23Z.

The writer that feeds app-189-metrics-timeseries stopped producing or shipping samples for about seven hours (after the 2026-11-22T00:23:00Z document, before the 07:23:00Z document); the index alone cannot show whether samples were never produced or were produced and not indexed, and no component in the examined evidence was identified as that writer.

Identify and inspect the component that writes app-189-metrics-timeseries, then compare its own logs and restart timestamps for 2026-11-22T00:23Z-07:23Z, and check Elasticsearch ingest/indexing health for the same interval, to determine whether the interruption was at collection/export or at indexing.

gaps: The cause of the seven-hour writing interruption (2026-11-22T00:23:00Z to 07:23:00Z) is not identified; no Kubernetes object, event or log line was observed applying a change or fault to the writer during that interval.

Prometheus could not be queried: metrics_range_query (operation d5f26d37-752c-440d-a5ab-7bf73968a132-t0) and execute_prometheus_instant_query (operation 0053856c-7184-417e-8e81-af0f935d6657-t0) both returned status error, reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so other telemetry from the same period could not be checked for a matching gap.

The otel-collector pod logs for 2026-11-22T00:20Z-07:30Z could not be read: fetch_pod_logs hit the 4 MiB read limit, read only through 2026-11-22T10:06:43.469931Z and dropped 12058 lines that fell after the query window end, so no log lines from the gap interval were examined.
Kubernetes events expire and the returned events cover only 2026-11-22T09:32:52Z-10:07:47Z (2 Endpoints/FailedToCreateEndpoint events); the event history for 2026-11-22T00:23Z-07:23Z is unknown.

The index reports 42 documents in total but only the 18 inside the authorized window were examined; documents before 2026-11-21T10:24:58Z lie outside the authorized window, so earlier collection gaps in this index are unknown.

The component that writes app-189-metrics-timeseries was not identified: a ConfigMap query over 20 configmaps for app-189 or metrics-timeseries and a Deployment query over 24 deployments for app-189, elasticsearch, indexer or exporter both returned no results.
Whether the metric samples were produced but not indexed, or never produced, cannot be distinguished from the index contents alone.

Pod restartCount values are current counters without timestamps, so restarts cannot be placed at 2026-11-22T00:23Z-07:23Z; the change_history integration is not available, so configuration changes to the writer cannot be reviewed.
next_steps: Locate the agent/export job for app-189-metrics-timeseries and read its logs and restart times for 2026-11-22T00:23Z-07:23Z.
Check Elasticsearch ingest/indexing health and any write rejections or backpressure for that index over the same interval.
Compare with other telemetry sources (Prometheus/traces) for 2026-11-22T01:00Z-07:00Z to see whether the interruption was specific to this index or cluster-wide, once Prometheus is reachable.
Confirm whether the anomalous request_id REQ-37-8A4F2 at 2026-11-22T00:23:00Z reflects a writer-side change at the moment the data stopped.
